item.content:
Day 15 - Making of Harry Potter / メイキング・オブ・ハリー・ポッター

Entrance / エントランス

Right after the Cursed Child play, I visited The Making of Harry Potter studio tour the next day. It was freaking hot outside—around 31°C! I really wanted to wear the Gryffindor cloak I bought back at USJ in Osaka, but I was way too shy. Man, I regret it so much… don’t even get me started. So many other fans were proudly wearing theirs!

「舞台ハリー・ポッターと呪いの子」を観劇した翌日、ワーナー ブラザース スタジオツアー東京 - メイキング・オブ・ハリー・ポッターに行ってきました。外はとにかく暑くて、気温は31℃くらい！大阪のUSJで買ったグリフィンドールのローブを着たくて持っていったのですが、恥ずかしがり屋が出てしまって着られませんでした…本当に後悔しています。だって周りのファンはみんな誇らしげに着ていたから！

In the park outside, we were greeted by statues of Hagrid and Harry. Entering the main building, there was a massive dragon hanging right from the ceiling. I skipped the main shop for now and headed straight into the tour.

屋外のパークでは、ハグリッドとハリーのスタチューが出迎えてくれました。メインビルディングに入ると、天井から巨大なドラゴンが吊り下げられていました。ショップは後回しにして、さっそくツアーへと向かいます。

Inside / ツアー内部へ

The walls were lined with giant poster displays from all the Harry Potter films. We gathered in front of a massive set of doors while the tour staff gave us an introduction on what to expect. She asked if anyone had a birthday coming up soon… but no one spoke up. Mine was just a month away, but shyness struck again and I kept quiet. I know, I know!!! Please kill me! 😭

壁にはハリー・ポッター全映画作品の巨大なポスターがずらりと並んでいました。ツアーのスタッフさんから見どころや注意事項のツアー案内を聞きながら、大きな扉の前に集まります。スタッフさんが「もうすぐ誕生日の方はいらっしゃいますか？」と尋ねてくれたのですが…誰も手を挙げませんでした。実は僕の誕生日はほんの1ヶ月後だったのですが、またしても人見知りを発動して黙ってしまいました。分かってます、分かってますってば！！！穴があったら入りたい！😭

After a few minutes, open sesame!

数分後、いざ、開けゴマ！

The Great Hall / 大広間

It was so stunning inside. We were literally walking right through the Great Hall! We saw the Sorting Hat, and as everyone gathered around, it came to life, speaking and calling out all four houses: Ravenclaw, Hufflepuff, Slytherin, and Gryffindor!

中は言葉を失うほど素晴らしかったです。本当に大広間の中を歩いているんです！組分け帽子が置いてあり、みんなが集まると帽子が動き出し、4つの寮（レイブンクロー、ハッフルパフ、スリザリン、グリフィンドール）の名前を呼び上げ始めました！

Hogwarts Sets & Architecture / ホグワーツのセット＆建築

Triwizard Tournament / 三大魔法学校対抗試合（トライウィザード・トーナメント）

Dumbledore’s Office / ダンブルドアの部屋

Potions Class / 魔法薬学の教室

Defense Against the Dark Arts Class / 闇の術に対する防衛術の教室

Charms Class / 妖精の魔法の教室

It’s LeviOsa, not Leviosaa!
「レヴィオーサ」だよ、「レヴィオサー」じゃない！

TOM MARVOLO RIDDLE aka I AM LORD VOLDEMORT / トム・マールヴォロ・リドル（またの名を ヴォルデモート卿）

The Forbidden Forest / 禁じられた森

Centaurs / ケンタウロス

Dementors / 吸魂鬼（ディメンター）

EXPECTO PATRONUM / エクスペクト・パトローナム（守護霊よ、来たれ）！

Aragog / アラゴグ

Hagrid’s Hut / ハグリッドの小屋

Halfway through, I bought a cup of Butterbeer and popcorn!
ツアーの折り返し地点で、バタービールとバタービール味のポップコーンを買いました！

Number 4, Privet Drive / プリベット通り4番地

Inside the Dursley house / ダーズリー家の中：

Cupboard Under the Stairs / 階段下の物置：

Flying Hogwarts Letters and Aunt Marge / 舞い散るホグワーツの入学許可書とマージおばさん：

Platform 9 ¾ / 9と¾番線

Inside the Hogwarts Express / ホグワーツ特急の車内：

Dementors / ディメンター：

Quick Story Time / こぼれ話

Right near the Hogwarts Express was a Harry Potter Shop. While I was browsing, one of the Japanese staff members noticed my hat and called out to me, saying, “Hey, cool hat!”

9と¾番線のすぐ近くにハリー・ポッターのショップがありました。グッズを見ていた時、日本人スタッフの方に帽子を見られて「あ、それ良い帽子ですね！」と声をかけられたんです。

I told him I’d gotten it at a concert the week before, and he got super excited, replying, “Eyy sugoi! I’m a big fan of Ado!”

「先週のライブで買ったんですよ」と答えると、その人は大興奮して「えっすごい！僕、Adoの大ファンなんです！」と言ってくれました。

He even showed me his Ado tattoo on his palm! We ended up chatting for 5–10 minutes about our favorite songs and concert moments. I totally forgot to show him the Ado fan map project I made, but it was such a fun encounter!

なんと手のひらにあるAdoのタトゥーまで見せてくれました！お気に入りの曲やライブの思い出について5〜10分ほど盛り上がりました。僕が作ったAdoファンマップのプロジェクトを見せるのをすっかり忘れてしまいましたが、本当に楽しい出会いでした！

Ministry of Magic / 魔法省

Behind the Scenes / 舞台裏・クリーチャー制作

Don’t forget to cover your ears… Mandrake alert!
耳をふさぐのを忘れずに…マンドレイク注意！

Monster Book of Monsters / 怪物的な怪物の本：

Goblins / ゴブリン（小鬼）：

Kreacher and Dobby / クリーチャーとドビー：

Weasleys’ Wizard Wheezes / ウィーズリー・ウィザード・ウィーズ（イタズラ専門店）：

End of the Road / ツアーの締めくくり

There was a tiny show, but the video was too long to upload… It was absolutely beautiful, though!
ちょっとしたショーもあったのですが、動画が長すぎてアップロードできませんでした…でも本当に美しかったです！

And that’s it for the Making of Harry Potter Studio Tour!
というわけで、スタジオツアー東京のレポートは以上です！

I bought a lot of stuff… a hoodie, the long-sleeve T-shirt Harry wore during the Triwizard Tournament (customized with my name on the back!), the Harry Potter sweater with the big ‘H’, a personalized passport holder, my Hogwarts Platform 9 ¾ ticket, and a ton of keychains and plushies.
散々グッズも買い込んじゃいました…パーカー、三大魔法学校対抗試合でハリーが着ていた背中に自分の名前が入ったカスタム長袖Tシャツ、胸に大きな「H」がついたハリーのセーター、名入れしたパスポートホルダー、9と¾番線のチケット、アドそして大量のキーホルダーやぬいぐるみ。

Mischief managed! 🪄 / いたずら完了！ 🪄

item.content:
Japan trip / 日本一人旅

Konnichiwa minna-san,

So, a dream finally came true after years and years of wondering if I would ever get here. It’s currently the first of July, and I am sitting in my hotel, Hotel Onyado Nono Kyoto Shichijo Natural Hot Spring, in Kyoto as I start writing this blog.

何年も何年も「いつか行けるのだろうか」と思い続けていた夢が、ついに叶いました。このブログを書き始めた今は7月1日。京都のホテル「天然温泉 蓮花の湯 御宿 野乃京都七条」の部屋に座っています。

Day 1 - 24th June / 1日目 - 6月24日

I arrived at Tokyo Haneda Airport around 11:00 PM after a 7-hour flight from Malaysia. The Tokyo night view from above was f***ing breathtaking. Not gonna lie, I shed a few tears when I saw that view.

マレーシアからの7時間のフライトを経て、午後11時頃に東京・羽田空港に到着しました。上空から見下ろす東京の夜景は息をのむほど美しかったです。嘘偽りなく、その景色を見た瞬間、思わず涙がこぼれました。

My itinerary looked like this:

  • Arrive in Tokyo -> Take domestic flight to Osaka -> Stay in Osaka -> Head to Kyoto for 2 days -> Return to Osaka -> Head back to Tokyo for the rest of the trip.

旅程はこんな感じです：

  • 東京到着 -> 国内線で大阪へ -> 大阪滞在 -> 京都へ（2日間） -> 大阪に戻る -> 残りの日程は東京へ。

Layover at Tokyo Haneda Airport / 羽田空港でのレイオーバー

I landed at Terminal 2 at 11:00 PM, and my connection to Osaka wasn’t until 8:00 AM the next morning. Back when I was planning, I thought, “Hey, I have a 9-hour transit! I can just walk around and collect some Eki Stamps.” Boy, was I wrong!

午後11時に第2ターミナルに着いたのですが、大阪行きの乗り継ぎ便は翌朝の8時でした。旅行の計画を立てていた時は、「9時間も乗り継ぎ時間があるから、歩き回って駅スタンプを集めよう！」なんて考えていたんです。…甘かった！

Basically, almost every Information Service desk—whether in the airport or railway stations has a unique stamp you can collect, but I completely forgot to check if they closed at night. I ended up spending the next 2 hours just wandering around a mostly quiet Terminal 2.

空港や駅の案内所にはオリジナルのスタンプが置いてあることが多いのですが、夜間に閉まるかどうかを確認するのを完全に忘れていました。結局、静まり返った第2ターミナルを2時間ほど彷徨う羽目になりました。

I got my personalized Suica card for the metro. Of course, I had to get my name printed on it!

地下鉄用に自分だけのMy Suica（記名式Suica）を発行しました。もちろん名前入りです！

There were plenty of vending machines around, and I was thirsty af, so I tried a drink called Pocari Sweat. I chugged the whole thing in under 2 minutes. It was so freaking good!

自動販売機がたくさんあって喉がカラカラだったので、「ポカリスエット」というドリンクを買ってみました。2分もかからずに一気に飲み干しました。めちゃくちゃ美味しかった！

Around midnight, a security guard came up to inform me that Terminal 2 was closing. (Wait, what?! I didn’t know airport terminals closed! Where the hell am I supposed to go? My whole plan was to crash at the terminal!).

夜の12時頃、警備員さんがやってきて「第2ターミナルは閉館します」と告げられました。（えっ、嘘でしょ！？空港のターミナルって夜閉まるの！？どこに行けばいいの？ターミナルで夜を明かす計画だったのに！）

He told me I needed to transfer over to Terminal 3. Apparently, Haneda shuts down Terminals 1 and 2 around midnight, so everyone has to head to Terminal 3 to rest until morning. So I hopped on the free airport interterminal shuttle bus and made my way over.

警備員さんによると、第3ターミナルへ移動する必要があるとのこと。羽田空港は深夜になると第1・第2ターミナルを閉鎖するため、朝まで休む人はみんな第3ターミナルへ向かうのだそうです。というわけで、無料のターミナル間連絡バスに乗って第3ターミナルへ向かいました。

Terminal 3 / 第3ターミナル

Terminal 3 was huge. My feet were completely dead, and I was pretty sure I had blisters forming, so I found a spot to sit down and rested for about an hour before heading out to explore again.

第3ターミナルはとても広かったです。足は限界で絶対にマメができている感触があったので、ベンチを見つけて1時間ほど休み、それから再び探検に出かけました。

At 2:00 AM, I went into Lawson and grabbed an egg sandwich, it was decent, nothing overly mind-blowing—and an onigiri.

午前2時、ローソンに入ってたまごサンド（普通に美味しかったですが感動するほどではなかったです）とおにぎりを買いました。

I went up to the 3rd floor, and holy shit, I was not expecting a giant Godzilla staring down at me from above!

3階に上がると、なんと巨大なゴジラが上から見下ろしていてビックリしました！

There was another one on the 2nd floor as well.

2階にももう一体いました。

I spent the rest of the night alternating between walking around and sitting on the benches. By the time morning rolled around, I had been awake for almost 24 hours straight!

それからは歩き回ったりベンチで休んだりを繰り返し、朝を迎える頃には丸24時間連続で起きている状態になっていました！

Day 2 - 25th June Osaka / 2日目 - 6月25日 大阪

At 6:00 AM, I waited until the Information Service desk opened and finally got my very first Eki Stamp! There were actually a few more on the upper floors, but since I was worried about missing my flight, I gave up on those and went straight to the free shuttle bus back to Terminal 2.

午前6時、案内所が開くのを待って、ついに記念すべき最初のスタンプをゲットしました！上の階にもいくつかスタンプがあったのですが、飛行機に乗り遅れるのが怖かったので諦め、無料 shuttle バスで第2ターミナルに戻りました。

Terminal 2 was absolutely bombarded with people as I entered, a huge contrast to last night, when it was completely empty! I checked in and headed straight to my gate. I was so excited to see Mount Fuji from the plane and had specifically booked a window seat just for the view. But guess what? Two nasty typhoons were hitting Japan, and as “lucky” as I am, it was completely cloudy so I didn’t get to see it at all!

昨夜のガラガラだった様子とは打って変わって、朝の第2ターミナルは大混雑！チェックインを済ませてゲートへ向かいました。機内から富士山を見るのをすごく楽しみにしていたので、わざわざ窓側の席を予約していたんです。しかし…なんと強烈な台風が2つも日本に接近しており、いつもの「運の良さ」を発揮して一面の曇り空。富士山は全く見えませんでした！

When I arrived at Osaka Itami/Kansai Airport, navigation was surprisingly easy. I went straight to the Information Service desk to pick up the Mobal eSIM I had pre-booked. There was also another Eki Stamp there, so of course, I collected that too. The lady at the counter was so sweet when I told her I was from Mauritius, she smiled and went, “Sugoi ne! I want to visit Mauritius too!”

大阪（伊丹/関空）に到着すると、移動は驚くほどスムーズでした。事前予約していたMobalのeSIMを受け取るために案内所へ向かいました。そこにもスタンプがあったので、もちろんゲット！カウンターの女性にモーリシャスから来たと伝えると、「すごいね！私もモーリシャスに行ってみたいです！」と笑顔で話してくれて、とても気さくな方でした。

At this point, I was so exhausted I could barely stand. During my initial planning, my idea was to take the subway to my hotel. However, the information lady recommended taking the airport limousine bus instead, as it dropped off right behind my hotel which was so much more convenient. So I took her advice!

この時点で僕は立っているのもやっとなくらい疲れていました。最初は地下鉄でホテルまで行くつもりだったのですが、案内所のスタッフさんが「リムジンバスならホテルのすぐ裏に着くからずっと便利ですよ」と勧めてくれたので、お言葉に甘えてバスに乗ることにしました！

APA Hotel & Exploring / APAホテルと散策

I arrived at my APA Hotel around 11:30 AM. I walked up to the check-in desk, only to be told that check-in didn’t open until 3:00 PM (15:00). Bruh!!!!! I could have literally cried. They mentioned that early check-in required an extra fee, so I decided to just drop off my luggage and go for a walk instead.

午前11時半頃にAPAホテルに到着。フロントへ向かうと「チェックインは午後3時（15:00）からです」と言われました。…マジかよ！！！泣きそうになりました。アーリーチェックインには追加料金がかかるとのことだったので、荷物だけ預けて散歩に出かけることにしました。

I was starving at this point. As I walked down the street, I spotted four Japanese salarymen heading into a nearby building. I decided to follow their lead and went into the exact same restaurant they entered!

お腹もペコペコでした。道を歩いていると、日本のサラリーマン4人が近くのビルに入っていくのを発見。「地元の人について行けば間違いない！」と思い、彼らと同じお店に入ってみました！

I sat down and ordered a Conger Eel (Anago) Bento Set, and it was so good! It came with cold soba, eel over rice (the sauce was amazing!), hot miso soup, and a side broth to mix with the soba.

席に着き「あなご弁当セット」を注文したのですが、これがめちゃくちゃ美味しかった！冷たいそば、あなご重（タレが絶品！）、温かいお味噌汁、そして蕎麦湯までついていました。

Since I wasn’t wearing a watch on this trip, I decided to hunt one up. I found a nearby Bic Camera store and ended up buying a Garmin watch. Bic Camera was massive about seven floors! I spent nearly two hours wandering around, mostly getting lost in the anime section, of course.

今回の旅行では腕時計をしてこな買ったので、時計を探すことにしました。近くのビックカメラに入り、Garminのスマートウォッチを購入。ビックカメラは7階建てくらいあってとにかく巨大！2時間近く店内を歩き回り、当然のごとくアニメコーナーで没頭してしまいました。

Evening in Dotonbori / 道頓堀の夜

By 3:00 PM, I finally checked into my room and immediately passed out for a much-needed rest.

午後3時、ようやくチェックインして即爆睡。必要な休息をとりました。

I woke back up around 9:00 PM (21:00) and headed out for a night walk through the city.

夜の9時頃に目を覚まし、夜の街へ散歩に出かけました。

I played my very first gachapon machine of the trip and got Hedwig!

旅で最初のガチャガチャに挑戦し、ヘドウィグをゲット！

Ayy, I finally saw the famous Glico Running Man sign in Dotonbori!

ついに道頓堀の有名なグリコサインを見ることができました！

I ended up spending around ¥1,200 on a crane game trying to win a Frieren figure… but left empty-handed 🥲.

フリーレンのフィギュアを狙ってクレーンゲームに1,200円ほど使ったのですが…手ぶらで終わりました🥲。

Universal Studios Japan (USJ) / ユニバーサル・スタジオ・ジャパン

Well, here we are, the moment I’ve been waiting for! But wait… of course there was a typhoon rolling in. See how lucky I am?

さあやってきました、待ちに待った瞬間！…と思いきや、当然のように台風が直撃。僕の運の良さ（？）がお分かりいただけるでしょう。

I walked down to the metro station only to be told that trains weren’t running due to the severe weather, and apparently, one of the main stations on the line was flooded! With no other option to get to the park, I had to get a taxi. It cost me around ¥5,000, but I wasn’t going to let a typhoon ruin my day at USJ.

地下鉄の駅まで歩いて行くと、悪天候のため電車が運転見合わせ、しかも路線上の主要駅が冠水しているとのこと！パークへ行く手段が他になく、タクシーを使うことにしました。約5,000円かかりましたが、台風ごときにUSJでの一日を台無しにされてたまるか！という思いでした。

The very first thing I did after walking through the gates was head straight to the Information Center to get my USJ Eki Stamp!

入園して真っ先に向かったのはインフォメーションセンター。USJのスタンプをしっかりゲットしました！

Detective Conan Show / 名探偵コナン ライブ・ショー

USJ is absolutely massive, and honestly, I didn’t really have a set plan for where to go first. I just walked toward the first attraction I saw, which happened to be the Detective Conan 4-D show.

USJはとにかく広くて、正直どこから回るか決めていませんでした。目に入った最初のアトラクションに向かったところ、それが「名探偵コナン」の4Dショーでした。

The pre-show had English subtitles on the side screens setting up the storyline, which made it super easy to follow along. The live host was so kawaii, and getting to see Kaito Kid make his dramatic appearance was so cool!

プレショーの画面には英語字幕が付いていたのでストーリーがすごく分かりやすかったです。MCの女性がとっても可愛くて、怪盗キッドが華麗に登場するシーンはめちゃくちゃカッコよかった！

Minion / ミニオン

After Conan, I wandered over to Minion Park. The ride was okay… not my favorite, but the vibrant decor and cute minion chaos still made it a lot of fun to walk through!

コナンの後はミニオン・パークへ。ライドアトラクションはまあ普通でしたが、カラフルな装飾と可愛らしいミニオンたちのハチャメチャな雰囲気は歩いているだけで楽しかったです！

The Flying Dinosaur / ザ・フライング・ダイナソー

Oh boy… while walking around, I could hear people on the ride screaming their absolute lungs out. I was so excited for this! Believe it or not, I had never been on a rollercoaster or theme park ride before in my life, so this was going to be my absolute first experience.

歩いていると、乗客の喉が千切れるほどの絶叫が聞こえてきました。これには大興奮！信じられないかもしれませんが、僕は人生で一度もジェットコースターに乗ったことがなかったので、これが生まれて初めての体験になります。

And holy hell, it did NOT disappoint! I could literally feel my soul coming out of my body on those drops, but I held it together and didn’t scream xD. It was literally one hell of a ride—now I completely understand why some people faint on these things!

そして…期待を裏切らない凄まじさでした！ 急降下するとき、文字通り魂が体から抜け出るような感覚がしましたが、なんとか堪えて叫ばずに済みました（笑）。本当に凄まじい絶叫マシンで、気を失う人がいる理由が心から理解できました！

P.S. I ended up riding it three times!
追記：結局3回も乗っちゃいました！

The Wizarding World of Harry Potter / ウィザーディング・ワールド・オブ・ハリー・ポッター

If you know me, you know I’ve been a massive Harry Potter fan since childhood. Stepping into Hogsmeade and seeing Hogwarts Castle looming in front of me was a huge moment. Even though I was standing there looking completely stone-faced on the outside, I was screaming with pure excitement on the inside!

僕を知っている人なら、僕が子供の頃から大のハリー・ポッターファンであることを知っているはず。ホグズミード村に足を踏み入れ、目の前にそびえ立つホグワーツ城を見た瞬間は感無量でした。外見はポーカーフェイスを装っていましたが、心の中では大興奮で叫びまくっていました！

Inside Hogwarts Castle / ホグワーツ城の内部

I didn’t manage to take too many pictures and videos inside, but it was exactly as magical as I expected. Seeing the Sorting Hat talk in person and walking through the castle hallways was incredible.

内部の写真はあまり撮れませんでしたが、期待通りの魔法のような世界でした。しゃべる組分け帽子を間近で見たり、城の廊下を歩いたりできて感動しました。

The queue for Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey was long, but thanks to the Express Pass, I got priority access and only waited about 10 minutes! The ride itself was amazing—seeing the flying Dementors up close was insane, and the Aragog spider scene actually jumpscared me!

「ハリー・ポッター・アンド・ザ・フォービドゥン・ジャーニー」の列は長蛇の列でしたが、エクスプレス・パスのおかげで10分ほどで乗れました！アトラクション自体も素晴らしく、間近で迫るディメンターやアラゴグ（巨大クモ）には本気でビクッとさせられました！

After Forbidden Journey, I jumped on the Flight of the Hippogriff coaster. Since it was outdoors, I rode the whole thing in the pouring rain!

その後は「フライト・オブ・ザ・ヒッポグリフ」へ。野外コースターなので、土砂降りの中で乗ることになりました！

Hagrid’s Hut / ハグリッドの小屋

I headed back to Hogsmeade to do some proper shopping and bought myself a Gryffindor house cloak!

ホグズミードに戻ってしっかり買い物をし、グリフィンドールのローブを購入！

I actually spent around 30 minutes chatting with one of the shop staff members. I showed her the plush Dodo I brought with me from Mauritius, and she taught me a few Japanese words, it was such a fun interaction!

ショップのスタッフさんと30分ほどおしゃべりをしました。モーリシャスから持ってきたドードー鳥のぬいぐるみを見せたら、日本語の単語をいくつか教えてくれて、とても楽しい交流になりました！

Frieren / 葬送のフリーレン

Next up, I went over to the Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End experience. Unlike the Conan show, this one didn’t have English subtitles, but I was totally fine following along in Japanese. I was the only foreigner in the entire group rocking my Gryffindor cloak among all the Japanese fans!

次は「葬送のフリーレン」のアトラクションへ。コナンと違って英語字幕はありませんでしたが、日本語で十分に楽しめました。日本のファンに混ざって、グリフィンドールのローブを着た外国人は僕一人だけでした！

Photography wasn’t allowed inside, but it was designed as an immersive journey following Frieren, Fern, and Stark. Frieren’s magic takes you on a walk through memories, and it was such a beautiful, atmospheric experience.

内部は撮影禁止でしたが、フリーレン、フェルン、シュタルクの旅を追体験できる素晴らしい没入型アトラクションでした。記憶を辿る魔法の世界観がとても美しく印象的でした。

And as always, Frieren can’t resist checking a chest…

Ah, the famous Super Nintendo World! As expected, it was completely packed with people. I went on some rides—it was super cool, but definitely crowded.

噂のスーパー・ニンテンドー・ワールド！予想通り大混雑でした。アトラクションにも乗りましたが、最高にクオリティが高い反面、とにかく人が多かったです。

ハリウッド・ドリームは迫力満点でしたが、「フライング・ダイナソー」ほど恐怖感はありませんでした。この頃には雨がかなり激しく降っていたため、降りる頃には全身ずぶ濡れになっていました！

Harry Potter Again / 再びハリー・ポッターへ

Around 6:00 PM, I made my way back to the Wizarding World one last time. I re-rode the attractions and hung around Hogsmeade until the evening lights turned on, illuminating Hogwarts Castle against the night sky—the perfect finish to a wild, typhoon-filled day at USJ!

午後6時頃、最後にもう一度魔法界へ。アトラクションに再び乗り、夜のライトアップで漆黒の夜空に浮かび上がるホグワーツ城を眺めました。台風に見舞われた荒れ模様の1日でしたが、最高の締めくくりとなりました！

I decided to keep it light on the weekend, so I focused more on doing some shopping at Uniqlo. The clothes there are so light and inexpensive.

週末は無理せずゆったり過ごすことにし、ユニクロでショッピングを楽しみました。軽くて安くて最高です。

Nipponbashi Denden Town / 日本橋でんでんタウン

Nipponbashi Denden Town is essentially the mini Akihabara of Osaka. As an otaku myself, I had to go! There were several buildings stacked with anime figures and merch. I specifically went on a hunt for the first volume of the One Piece manga, which is surprisingly hard to find. After searching through almost every single store, I finally found it!

日本橋でんでんタウンは、まさに大阪のミニ秋葉原。オタクである僕が行かないわけにはいきません！フィギュアやアニメグッズが詰まったビルがいくつもありました。特に『ONE PIECE』の単行本1巻を探していたのですが、これが意外と見つからない！ほぼ全店舗を回って、ついにゲットできました！

I ended up grabbing a whole stack of manga, including One Piece, Frieren, Jujutsu Kaisen, and Attack on Titan.

結局、『ONE PIECE』『葬送のフリーレン』『呪術廻戦』『進撃の巨人』など、マンガを大量買いしてしまいました。

HARUKAS 300 × Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End / あべのハルカス300 × 葬送のフリーレン

About a week before coming to Japan, I found out that the HARUKAS 300 observation deck was having a collaboration with Frieren. Naturally, I knew I had to go!

日本に来る1週間ほど前、あべのハルカス300の展望台で『葬送のフリーレン』のコラボイベントが開催されていることを知り、「絶対に行かなきゃ！」と思っていました。

Funny story: when I checked Google Maps, it said it was only 3.3 km away. Silly me thought, “Hey, I can easily walk that!” So I did… and it felt like an absolute eternity. But no regrets at all, because I got to see some really cool scenery along the way.

笑い話なのですが、Googleマップで調べたら距離がたった3.3kmと表示されたんです。愚かな僕は「これなら余裕で歩けるじゃん！」と思い歩き始めたのですが…果てしなく遠く感じました（笑）。でも途中で素敵な街並みを見られたので後悔はありません！

The view from the top was breathtaking.

展望台からの景色は息をのむ美しさでした。

I stayed until it got dark for the Frieren projection mapping show. They even had a special Frieren stamp rally event!

暗くなるまで待って、フリーレンのプロジェクションマッピングを鑑賞。スタンプラリーイベントも楽しめました！

I definitely took the subway on the way back! Ended the day with a massive 32k steps completed.

帰りは迷わず地下鉄に乗りました！この日は合計3万2千歩も歩いていました。

Day 10 - First Day in Shinjuku, Tokyo (Pre-Ado Concert) / 10日目 - 東京・新宿初日（Adoライブ前日）

Finally, the day I’ve been waiting for!

ついに、待ちに待った日がやってきました！

I woke up around 8:00 AM, and since checkout was at 10:00 AM, I got straight to organizing my luggage. Carrying a massive suitcase with me all the way from Osaka to Tokyo would have been a complete pain in the back. Thankfully, my hotel offered luggage forwarding! I went down to the lobby around 9:30 AM, and the staff member there was super friendly and helpful. I provided him with my next hotel details, and the total cost for forwarding was around ¥2,000.

朝8時頃に起き、10時のチェックアウトに向けて荷物整理を開始。大阪から東京まで巨大なスーツケースを持ち運ぶのは絶対に腰が死ぬので、ホテルの宅急便サービス（荷物配送）を利用しました。9時半頃ロビーへ行くと、スタッフさんがとても親切に対応してくれ、次のホテルの住所を伝えて約2,000円で送ることができました！

To get from Osaka to Tokyo, I took the Shinkansen (the bullet train). I had already booked my ticket prior to arriving in Japan. While waiting on the platform, I noticed several other fans wearing Ado merch!

大阪から東京への移動は新幹線を利用。日本に到着する前に予約しておきました。ホームで待っていると、Adoのライブグッズを着たファンを何人も見かけました！

Ado was actually holding a two-day concert at Nissan Stadium in Yokohama, and I was lucky enough to secure a ticket for the second day. I initially thought I had bought a ticket for the first day, but after triple-checking my confirmation email later on, I realized it was actually for day two. Anyway… I really wanted to go to the first day’s show as well, but Ticketboard was only selling day two tickets when I checked—which sucked because I already had one for that day!

Adoは横浜の日産スタジアムで2日間のライブを開催しており、僕は幸運にも2日目のチケットを確保できていました。最初は1日目のチケットを買ったと思い込んでいたのですが、後で確認メールを何度も見返したら2日目でした（笑）。1日目も行きたかったのですが、僕がチェックした時にはTicketboardで2日目しか売っていなかったので断念しました。

Anyway, I hopped on the Shinkansen. If you remember from earlier when I flew into Japan, I booked a seat specifically to catch a view of Mount Fuji, but couldn’t because of the typhoon. Well, I made sure to book the Mount Fuji side for this train ride, too. BUT GUESS WHAT?? MOUNT FUJI WAS SHY AGAIN! I didn’t get to see it fully just a tiny bit of the tip peaking out through the clouds.

新幹線に乗り込みました。飛行機の時と同じく、今回も富士山が見える側の席をバッチリ予約していたのですが…なんと今回も富士山はシャイでした！雲の間からほんの少しだけてっぺんが見えただけでした（泣）。

I got off the Shinkansen at Tokyo Station and transferred to the subway to head to Shinjuku. Surprisingly, even though I had fully prepared myself to get completely lost inside Shinjuku Station, navigating to the exit was actually pretty straightforward!

東京駅で新幹線を降り、地下鉄に乗り換えて新宿へ。新宿駅のダンジョンで完全に迷子になる覚悟をしていましたが、意外にもスムーズに出口まで辿り着けました！

By the time I made it out, it was already around 3:00 PM (15:00), so I went straight to my hotel to check in. I stayed at the Shinjuku Prince Hotel, which was included in the official JTB travel package I booked to secure my concert ticket.

外に出るとすでに午後3時（15:00）を過ぎていたので、そのままホテルへ向かってチェックイン。ライブチケットを確保するために申し込んだJTBの公式ツアーパッケージに含まれていた新宿プリンスホテルに宿泊しました。

I stopped by the JTB desk in the lobby to pick up my concert ticket and to my surprise, they also handed me a bundle of bonus concert goodies! Major kudos to them!

ロビーのJTBデスクでチケットを受け取ると、サプライズでライブの限定特典グッズのセットも手渡されました！素晴らしい対応に大感謝です！

I had a quick chat with the JTB staff since my forwarded luggage wouldn’t be arriving until the next day. I wanted to double-check if they could store my bags after checkout, since I’d be leaving early for the concert. He went ahead and confirmed with the hotel staff, who happily agreed to hold my luggage until I returned!

大阪から送った荷物が翌日まで届かないため、ライブ当日のチェックアウト後に荷物を預かってもらえるかJTBスタッフさんに相談しました。ホテル側に確認をとってくれ、快く荷物を預かってくれることになりました！

The view from my room on the 16th floor was mindblowing, I could even see the famous Godzilla head right from my window!

16階の部屋からの眺めは最高で、窓からはなんと有名なゴジラヘッドが見えました！

For dinner that night, I went to Ichiran Ramen.

この日の夕食は一蘭のラーメンへ！

Day 11 - Day of the Concert / 11日目 - ライブ当日

Ahhhhh!!! The day is finally here!

あぁぁぁ！！！ついにこの日がやってきた！！

Yesterday was Day 1 of the concert, and I successfully managed to avoid every single setlist spoiler online. However, I found out that fans both yesterday and today were already queuing up as early as 6:00 AM. What are you guys doing?! The concert doesn’t even start until 6:00 PM (18:00)! But then again… what do I know? This was my very first time attending a concert in my entire life! I also saw that Adidas was selling a special FIFA x Ado collaboration jersey. I wanted to get one so badly, but it sold out almost instantly.

昨日の1日目のセットリストのネタバレをネットで一切見ずに回避成功！しかし、ファンが朝の6時から物販列に並んでいることを知りました。開演は夕方の6時（18:00）なのに、みんな凄すぎるよ…！まあ、人生初ライブの僕が言えたことではありませんが（笑）。アディダスのFIFA × Adoコラボユニフォームも欲しかったのですが、一瞬で完売してしまったようです。

I left my hotel around noon to head over to Yokohama, where the concert was being held and boy, I did NOT expect to get lost as many times as I did. I took the train towards Yokohama Station, intending to transfer to the line heading toward Shin-Yokohama Station near Nissan Stadium. But somehow, I don’t even know how I managed it, I completely messed up the transfer and ended up in places I’d never even heard of!

正午頃にホテルを出て、会場のある横浜へ向かいました。…が、まさかあんなに迷子になるとは思いもしませんでした。横浜駅で新横浜駅方面の電車に乗り換える予定だったのですが、どう間違えたのか全く聞いたこともない場所に着いてしまいました！

Eventually, I spotted a few Ado fans in merch and decided my best strategy was to just follow them. After taking two more subway lines, I finally, finally arrived at Nissan Stadium. It was quite a long walk from the station to the venue, and my god… there were SO many people. I mean A LOT!!!

最終的にライブグッズを着たファンを発見し、「あの人たちについて行けば間違いない！」と尾行作戦を決行。地下鉄をさらに2つ乗り継ぎ、ついに日産スタジアムに到着しました！駅から会場までは結構歩きましたが、とにかく人の数が凄まじかったです！！！

ドードーさん、Adoちゃんにご挨拶！

I walked around the stadium area until 2:00 PM (14:00) while waiting for general merchandise sales to open at 3:00 PM (15:00). I managed to get almost everything I wanted! The only thing I missed out on was the T-shirt, which unfortunately sold out in my size. But I was so hyped to finally get my hands on the official penlight!

午後3時からの一般物販開始を待ちつつ、スタジアム周辺を散策。欲しかったグッズのほとんどを手に入れることができました！自分のサイズのTシャツだけ売り切れてしまいましたが、公式ペンライトをゲットできて最高にハイテンションでした！

Treated myself to some Ado-themed beef dish before the big event!

開演前にAdoコラボの牛肉丼で腹ごしらえ！

スタジアム内部はめちゃくちゃ広い！！！僕の席は東スタンド 2列 131番。ステージからは少し距離がありましたが、会場全体が見渡せる良い席でした。

Phantom Siita / ファントムシータ

Their facial expressions and stage presence were so incredible to watch live!

午後5時（17:00）、オープニングアクトとしてファントムシータが登場。圧巻のパフォーマンスでした！約30分間のライブで、大好きな曲「ゾクゾク」を最後に歌ってくれて大興奮。生で見せる表情やパフォーマンスの存在感が凄すぎました！

That evening, I was invited out for Yakiniku by a local Japanese host. Actually, let me rephrase that… I was invited to do an interview! その日の夜、日本人のホストの方から焼肉に招待されました。というか、正確にはYouTubeインタビューの撮影でした！数日前、「日本食を食べるグルメインタビューに出演しませんか？」とDMをもらい、もちろん即答でOKしました！

超高級店で、テーブルの中央にグリルがある完全個室。普通の焼肉店なら自分で肉を焼きますが、そこは専属のシェフが目の前で極上のお肉を一枚ずつ焼いてくれるスタイルでした！

He set up his camera and started recording. The first dish brought out was beef tartare and goodness me, it was freaking delicious. Absolute magic in my mouth! 全てのメニューは覚えていませんが、写真を見る限りA5ランク和牛のカツサンドもあり、とんでもない美味しさでした。

続いてシェフが様々な部位を焼いてくれました。牛タンや、一口食べた瞬間に口の中でとろける極上和牛を堪能。

終盤にはご飯の上に牛肉とウナギが乗った料理が出ました。少し塩味が薄く感じたので、これだけは唯一あまり好みではありませんでした。

For dessert, we were served a matcha wafer sandwich with vanilla ice cream inside.

デザートはバニラアイスを挟んだ抹茶モナカ。

YouTubeにアップされているのですが…ここには載せません！（笑）

休憩含めて約5時間の長丁場でしたが、一秒たりとも無駄のない最高の体験でした。

お昼ごはんはカツカレーとお味噌汁…めちゃ美味！

I decided to try my luck at the game centers… and after way too many attempts (please don’t ask me how much money I spent on this 💀), I FINALLY won a Frieren figurine!

ゲームセンターでクレーンゲームに挑戦…（いくら使ったかは聞かないでください💀）、ついにフリーレンのフィギュアを自力でゲット！！

Day 18 - Akihabara (Part 2) / 18日目 - 秋葉原（パート2）

Had a huge crush on Mai Valentine from Yu-Gi-Oh! back in the day…

昔『遊戯王』の孔雀舞（マイ）が大好きだったんですよね…

FOUND ADO-CHANNN!!! 💙 Unfortunately, it was only CDs this time around!

Adoちゃん発見！！！💙 今回はCDコーナーでした！

MORE ADO-CHANNN!!!!

さらにAdoちゃん！！

While browsing in Animate, I stumbled upon the Your Name light novel/manga box set in English! Bought them without hesitation—snagged all three volumes!

アニメイトで英語版『君の名は。』の小説・ラノベボックスセットを発見！迷わず全3巻を即買い！

Also bought a giant (well, not that giant) Luffy figure!

ルフィの大きなフィギュアも購入！

Day 19 - Shibuya / 19日目 - 渋谷

Ah, Shibuya—the final stop of my trip! For as long as I can remember, I’ve watched the Shibuya Crossing live stream on YouTube, so actually being there felt surreal.

旅の最後の滞在地、渋谷！ずっとYouTubeで渋谷スクランブル交差点のライブカメラを見ていたので、実際にその場所に立っているのが夢のようでした。

Honestly though, I think Shibuya Crossing is a bit overrated. Every time the pedestrian light turns green, a bunch of people rush to the middle to pose for photos—mostly influencers! With so many crowds around, I was starting to get a bit irritated (I guess that’s why I travel alone! xD).

ただ正直言うと、スクランブル交差点はちょっとオーバーレイテッド（期待されすぎ）かなと（笑）。信号が青になるたびにインフルエンサーたちが中央に群がってポーズを決めるので、人が多すぎて少々イライラしちゃいました（だから一人旅が好きなんです！）。

Anyway, I even took a screenshot from the YouTube live stream to see if I could spot myself in the crowd!

ライブカメラのスクリーンショットを撮って、群衆の中に自分が映っているか探してみました！

Next, I headed to the Adidas Shibuya Store. Previously, they had a giant Ado wallpaper display set up inside, but it looks like they recently replaced it with a massive football jersey display!

続いてアディダス渋谷店へ。以前は巨大なAdoの壁面ディスプレイがあったのですが、サッカーユニフォームのディスプレイに変更されていました。

Here was the original giant Ado display from before:

以前の伝説的なAdoディスプレイがこちら：

I went inside really hoping to pick up both the white and short-sleeve Japan national team jerseys… but guess what? Sold out everywhere across Japan! What the hell?! I was so relieved I managed to snag the long-sleeve version back in Osaka.

日本代表の白ユニフォームと半袖ユニフォームを買いに入ったのですが、見事に全国完売！大阪で長袖を買っておいて本当に良かった…！

On the way, I even ran into a Paolo from TOKYO branded vending machine! If you don’t know him, he’s a YouTuber I’ve been watching for years who makes awesome videos on Japanese food and daily life. Definitely give his channel a watch!

移動中、長年観ているYouTuber「Paolo from TOKYO」さんのラッピング自販機に遭遇！日本のグルメや日常を紹介している素晴らしいチャンネルなのでオススメです！

Day 20 - Ginza Uniqlo Shopping / 20日目 - 銀座ユニクロ爆買い

Here is my breakfast from Lawson. Don’t judge me—it was freaking good!

ローソンで買った朝食。笑わないでください、これがめちゃくちゃ美味しいんです！

Today, I decided to head to Ginza, home to a massive Uniqlo flagship store.

今日はユニクロの巨大グローバル旗艦店がある銀座へ。

I did a lot of shopping! For lunch, I checked out a local ramen spot with great reviews, and it was obviously super delicious.

服を爆買い！ランチは評判のラーメン店へ行きましたが、期待通りの絶品でした。

I also bought a new suitcase for a decent price back in Akihabara. I ended up buying a bunch of travel stickers and started sticking them all over it!

秋葉原でお手頃な新しいスーツケースを購入していたので、ステッカーをたくさん買ってペタペタ貼り始めました！

Day 21 - Ghibli Museum + Meiji Shrine / 21日目 - ジブリ美術館 ＆ 明治神宮

Ghibli Museum / 三鷹の森ジブリ美術館

GHIBLI DAYYY!!! Finally!

ついにジブリの日！！待ちに待った！

If you don’t know, getting tickets for the Ghibli Museum is ridiculously hard. Tickets go on sale on the 10th of every month at 10:00 AM Japan Standard Time (JST) for the following month. For me back home in Mauritius, that meant logging on at 5:00 AM.

ジブリ美術館のチケットを取るのがどれほど困難かご存知でしょうか。毎月10日の午前10時（日本時間）に翌月分のチケットが販売されるのですが、モーリシャス時間だと早朝の午前5時になります。

For four months straight leading up to the trip, I practiced getting into the queue! I would wake up at 4:00 AM just to test my strategy so I’d be 100% prepared when the June 10th tickets (for my July visit) went live.

旅行前の4ヶ月間、毎月10日に早朝4時に起きてチケット購入キューに並ぶシミュレーション訓練を重ねました！7月訪問分のチケットが発売される6月10日に万全の体制で挑むためです。

My battle setup: laptop + phone, running multiple browsers, dozens of tabs, and incognito windows active simultaneously. I literally had over 100 tabs open just to beat the queue system!

ノートPC＋スマホをフル活用し、複数ブラウザ、シークレットウィンドウ、100以上のタブを開いてシステムに挑みました！

Here are a few screenshots from my trial runs:

シミュレーションのスクショがこちら：

February 10th / 2月10日

March 10th / 3月10日

April 10th / 4月10日

I forgot to do the trial run in April!
4月は予行演習をうっかり忘れました！

May 10th / 5月10日

127,237th in the queue. Bloody hell!!
待ち順 127,237番。マジかよ！！

Finally, on the 10th of June, luck was on my side! Using my phone, I got placed 426th in the queue and was finally able to secure my ticket!

そして本番の6月10日、スマホで奇跡の426番を引き当て、ついにチケットを獲得できました！

The museum is located in Mitaka. On the day of the visit, I took two train lines: the Yamanote Line and the Chuo Line. From Mitaka Station, you need to catch a bus to the museum, but it’s super easy to navigate thanks to clear signs in English guiding you to the bus stop. If you’re lucky, you might get to ride the special yellow Ghibli Museum bus! (I wasn’t so lucky, though). The total journey took around 40 minutes.

美術館は三鷹にあります。山手線と中央線に乗って三鷹駅へ。駅からバスに乗るのですが、英語案内が分かりやすくてスムーズでした。運が良ければ黄色のジブリバスに乗れます！（僕は普通のバスでした泣）。移動は約40分。

I booked the 10:00 AM entry slot. I arrived right on time, and there was already a huge queue waiting to get inside.

10:00の初回枠を予約。時間通り到着するとすでに大行列でした。

The museum exterior:

美術館の外観：

At the entrance, after showing your QR code, you receive some special souvenirs. I got a physical 35mm film strip ticket featuring a scene from Ponyo—and everyone receives a different film frame! Inside the lobby, there’s even a projector setup where you can view your film strip on a backlit screen.

受付でQRコードを見せると、入場特典として『崖の上のポニョ』の35mm映画フィルムの入場券がもらえました！人によってカットが違い、ロビーには光にかざしてフィルムを見られる装置もありました。

Unfortunately, taking photos or videos inside the museum is strictly prohibited. To describe it briefly, the interior shows the magic of animation behind the scenes: zoetropes, traditional animation machinery, rooms covered wall-to-wall in concept sketches, and even a replica of Hayao Miyazaki’s desk! If you’re a fan of Studio Ghibli movies, definitely add this to your Japan travel plan—just make sure you prep for the ticket drop!

館内は完全撮影禁止。アニメーションの仕組みや制作舞台裏、パラパラ漫画の立体版（ゾトロープ）、スケッチで埋め尽くされた部屋や宮﨑駿監督のデスクの再現など、ジブリファンなら絶対に訪れるべき夢のような空間でした！

The souvenir shop is on the top floor. They had a lot of cool merch, though many items were a bit pricey. I ended up buying two small plushies: Totoro and a Soot Sprite.

最上階のショップ「マンマユート」でトトロとマックロクロスケの小さなぬいぐるみを購入。

Here is the museum seen from the outside garden area:

中庭から見上げた館外の風景：

On the roof garden, you’ll find the life-sized statue of the Robot Soldier from Laputa: Castle in the Sky:

屋上庭園には『天空の城ラピュタ』の実物大ロボット兵が！

Nearby, you’ll also find the Laputan Keystone (Control Cube) covered in ancient inscriptions from the movie:

ラピュタの要石（黒い石）も発見：

Spotted Baron and characters from The Cat Returns peering out through one of the windows!

窓から『猫の恩返し』のバロンたちが覗いているのを発見！

Meiji Shrine / 明治神宮

After the Ghibli Museum, I took the train over to Harajuku to visit Meiji Shrine. It was freaking hot out, and I was sweating like crazy! Thankfully, the pathway leading up to the shrine is fully shaded by a dense canopy of trees.

ジブリ美術館の後は原宿へ移動し明治神宮へ。とにかく猛暑で汗だくになりましたが、参道は鬱蒼とした木々に覆われていて涼しかったです。

Day 22 - Day Out of the City: Todoroki Valley / 22日目 - 都会のオアシス：等々力渓谷

Todoroki Ravine Park is a beautiful, quiet, and cool oasis tucked away right in Tokyo. I stumbled across this place by accident while browsing online and decided to check it out!

東京の真っ只中にこんな静かで涼しい癒やしの空間があるなんて！ネットで見つけて立ち寄ってみた等々力渓谷公園です。

Back to Shibuya / 渋谷へ戻る

I headed back to Shibuya after spending around 2 to 3 hours wandering through the valley.

2〜3時間散策した後、渋谷へ戻りました。

Had this for lunch:

ランチに食べたもの：

Next, I went to the ONE PIECE Mugiwara Store!

続いて「ONE PIECE 麦わらストア」へ！

I WANTED ALL OF THEM!!! 🏴‍☠️

全部欲しい！！！🏴‍☠️

I even got a commemorative store stamp for my logbook!

記念スタンプもバッチリ押しました！

Day 23 - Back to Akihabara: Steins;Gate Exhibition / 23日目 - 再び秋葉原：シュタインズ・ゲート展

I headed back to Akihabara for the special Steins;Gate exhibition. It took me a while to locate the right building, but I eventually made it!

『STEINS;GATE（シュタインズ・ゲート）』の特別展を見るために再び秋葉原へ。ビルを探すのに少し迷いましたが無事到着！

Day 24 - Relax Day - Last Day of Shopping / 24日目 - のんびり最終買い物日

Back in Shibuya, a wild Reggie from JJK appeared out of nowhere! It was actually a giant, 2-meter-tall statue of him. His body was completely covered in paper receipts. If you don’t know, Reggie is a character from Jujutsu Kaisen whose cursed technique, Contract Recreation, allows him to burn receipts to instantly manifest whatever item or service is printed on them into reality. For this event, you could actually step up and pull a receipt attached to the giant Reggie for a chance to win some amazing prizes!

渋谷で『呪術廻戦』のレジィ・スターの巨大スタチューを発見！全身レシートだらけのレジィから実際にレシートを破り取って豪華賞品が当たるイベントをやっていました！

I ended up waiting in queue for about an hour just to try it out. I actually won something! It was related to Monster Strike, but with the massive crowd, claiming the prize meant waiting another 2 to 3 hours. I decided not to bother and just kept moving, but it was still a super cool event to stumble upon.

1時間ほど並んで体験し、見事に賞品（モンスト関連）が当選！ただ引換にさらに2〜3時間待ちと言われたので諦めましたが、面白いイベントでした。

A long-time dream finally came true! The only downside? I had no one to do the iconic pose with on the steps xD, but it was still totally worth the visit!

長年の夢だった『君の名は。』の聖地の階段へ！一緒に例のポーズをする相手がいなかったことだけが心残りですが（笑）、来られて本当に感動しました！

Day 25 - Daihatsu Japan Open 2026 - Tokyo Metropolitan Gymnasium / 25日目 - ダイハツジャパンオープン2026（東京体育館）

My trip to Japan wasn’t originally supposed to be this long. But when I found out that the Japan Open was happening, I told myself I had to be there no matter what, so I extended my stay by another week. Luckily, I had already managed to secure a ticket to the finals back home in Mauritius.

元々の予定を1週間延長してまで観に来たダイハツジャパンオープン！モーリシャスにいる時に決勝のチケットを事前確保していました。

There were so many top players I was dying to see live, like An Se Young, Akane Yamaguchi, Chiharu Shida, Tomoka Miyazaki, etc. Unfortunately, Se-young had to withdraw due to injury, Shida didn’t participate, and Miyazaki lost in the first round. However, Yamaguchi made it all the way to the final, and I was beyond excited to watch her!

アン・セヨン、山口茜、志田千陽、宮崎友花など見たい選手が目白押しでした。怪我や欠場、敗退もありましたが、大好きな山口茜選手が決勝に進出して大興奮！

I arrived around 10:30 AM, and the venue was already packed with fans.

午前10:30頃到着。会場はファンで埋め尽くされていました。

View from my seat:

自分の座席からの眺め：

A hand fan featuring signatures from the Japanese national team players!

日本代表選手のサイン入りうちわ！

Mixed Doubles / 混合ダブルス

First up was the Mixed Doubles final featuring China vs. Chinese Taipei.

まずは中国 vs チャイニーズ・タイペイの混合ダブルス決勝。フルセットの熱戦の末、中国ペアが勝利！

Women’s Singles / 女子シングルス

Next up was the Women’s Singles! I’ve been a massive fan of Akane Yamaguchi for a long time and have watched almost every single one of her matches live on the BWF channel. Finally getting to see her play in person meant the world to me.

続いて女子シングルス！長年ずっと応援している山口茜選手のプレーを生で見られて最高に幸せでした。

Her opponent was Pusarla V. Sindhu.

対戦相手はプサルラ・V・シンドゥ選手。

The atmosphere inside the stadium was unbelievable.

会場の熱気が凄まじかったです。

Unfortunately, Akane didn’t manage to pull off the win, but Sindhu’s play was incredibly sharp and aggressive. She took the match in two straight sets.

残念ながら山口選手は破れてしまいましたが、シンドゥ選手の攻撃的なプレーが見事でした。

Men’s Singles / 男子シングルス

Next was Christo Popov vs. Koki Watanabe.

クリスト・ポポフ vs 渡辺航貴。ポポフ選手が絶好調でストレート勝ち。

Women’s Doubles / 女子ダブルス

Women’s Doubles featured the Korean pair Kim Hye Jeong and Kong Hee Yong vs. the Chinese pair Zhang Shu Xian and Jia Yi Fan.

韓国ペア vs 中国ペアの女子ダブルス。これが歴史に残る超絶怒涛の神試合となりました！

This match went to a deciding third set, and honest to God, we were treated to absolute peak badminton.

ファイナルセットにもつれ込み、バドミントン史に残る激闘へ。

The third set went deep into extra points: 20-20, 21-20, 21-21… all the way up to 26-26, 27-27!

20-20からデュースが延々と続き、26-26、27-27まで突入！

The photographers courtside added so much unintentional comedy to the moment. Every time the Korean pair held match point, all the photographers would shuffle back and forth (aller-retour) to focus on them, and the second the Chinese pair pulled ahead, they’d all hurry back to the other side to cover them instead. Watching them switch back and forth on every single point was hilarious!

コート脇のカメラマンたちが、マッチポイントが入れ替わるたびに右へ左へゾロゾロ移動する姿がコントみたいで面白かったです（笑）。

The match finally reached the ultimate sudden-death point at 29-29! On the final rally, Zhang Shu Xian hit a shot over the baseline; she initially thought she won the match, while the Korean pair immediately celebrated, knowing it was out. Absolute drama until the very last second! China called for a Hawk-Eye challenge, but the review confirmed the shuttle was out, handing the victory to the Korean pair.

最後は脅威の29-29のサドンデス！最後のラリーでシャトルがアウトになり、チャレンジの末、韓国ペアが奇跡的な勝利を収めました！

What a match! If you want to watch the full replay, here’s the link.

最高の試合でした！フルリプレイのリンクはこちら。

Men’s Doubles / 男子ダブルス

Finally, we had the Men’s Doubles final featuring Indonesia’s Fajar Alfian and Muhammad Shohibul Fikri against the world number one Korean pair, Kim Won Ho and Seo Seung Jae.

最後は男子ダブルス。世界ランク1位の韓国ペア相手に、インドネシアペアが凄まじいプレーで見事なジャイアントキリング（金星）を果たしました！

Day 26 - Final Day / 26日目 - 最終日

Ahhh… why can’t we have unlimited happiness? 😭

あぁぁ…幸せな時間はずっと続かないのでしょうか？😭

On my final day, I booked a taxi to drive me to the station for the Limousine Bus to Narita Airport. Technically, the bus stop was only about a 5min walk from my hotel, but it involved going down a set of stairs. Since I was hauling two huge pieces of luggage plus a massive backpack, I decided to take a taxi instead. It ended up being a quick 3min drive 😂, but I still paid 1,000 yen!

成田空港行きのリムジンバス乗り場へ向かうためタクシーを手配。徒歩5分の距離でしたが大荷物だったのでタクシーを使いました。3分で着いて1,000円でした（笑）。

I arrived at the stop, waited about an hour for the bus, and then headed off to the airport.

バスを待って空港へ出発。

This was the moment where I nearly cried… Honestly, Japan was so amazing. How I wish I lived here!

この瞬間、本気で泣きそうになりました…日本は本当に素晴らしかった。ここに住めたらどんなにいいか！

Day 27 - Layover in Malaysia / 27日目 - マレーシアでのレイオーバー

Well… back in Malaysia. Everything felt so noisy and chaotic, and I was getting irritated by every little thing after leaving Japan!

マレーシアに到着。日本を出た直後だったので、周囲の騒々しさやカオスさに少しイライラしてしまいました（笑）。

I landed in Malaysia around midnight, and my connecting flight wasn’t for another 12 hours (at 12:50 PM).

深夜に着き、次の乗り継ぎ便まで12時間。

I booked a capsule hotel right at the airport to get some sleep, refreshed myself, and then caught my flight back home.

空港内のカプセルホテルで睡眠をとり、リフレッシュして帰国便へ。

Saying goodbye to Japan was so hard, but this trip was everything I could have wished for and more. The countdown to the next trip starts now! 🎌

日本とお別れするのは寂しかったですが、思い描いていた以上の最高の旅になりました。次の旅へのカウントダウンが今始まります！🎌

Thinking of doing Mt. Fuji next time and going to see all the Mugiwaras Statues in Kumamoto Prefecture!

次は富士山登頂と、熊本県の麦わらの一味の像めぐりを計画中です！

item.content:
Ohayo! It’s been a while since I’ve written a blog post. I wanted to share an update on a project I’ve been working on for the past few months.

If you’ve never heard of her, Ado is a Japanese singer and Utaite (a singer who performs covers and original songs online). I’ve been a huge fan since she performed the songs for the One Piece Film: Red movie, where she provided the singing voice for Uta (Shanks’ daughter). Ever since then, I’ve been following her journey. She has never revealed her face. I actually hope she keeps her identity a secret…you never know how the public might react, and it adds to her unique mystique.

The Project: AdoVerse

The project I’ve been building is called AdoVerse. It is a fan community platform where fans can add their location to a global map. Many people might feel like they are the only ones in their country who listen to Ado, I created this website to show how massive the community truly is and how far her music has reached.

For example, I am from Mauritius. No one expects someone from this tiny island to be a fan! I really hope that one day Ado gets to see this project and realizes just how many fans she has worldwide.

The project is still in its early stages, but you can check it out here: https://adoverse.com/. I plan to add more features in the future to improve the experience for everyone.

How it works

Blue Roses

When you open the site, you’ll see a map covered in blue roses. Each rose represents a fan. I’ve used a clustering system, when you zoom out, the roses group together to show the total number of fans in a country or region. As you zoom in, the clusters expand, allowing you to see the locations more clearly.

Adding your location

To add your own spot on the map, simply click “Join the AdoVerse.” You can add your country, city (optional), and other details. You can also choose to keep your information private by selecting “Adonymous” (get it?) or make it public by linking your Instagram or X (Twitter) profile.

Concert countdown

One cool feature I added is a countdown for her upcoming concerts. If you click on a concert, the map will direct you straight to that location.

Past Concert

I’ve also included locations from her past tours so you can see everywhere she has performed so far.

Future plans

I plan to change the domain to adoverse.com or something similar soon. Also in the pipeline, i want to add a library for all her songs where new fans can easily see her songs.

Onions in Australia?

Ohh, you might be wondering why are onions flying around australia…hmmmm….welll, if you know..you know xD

P.S I am going to her Nissan Stadium concert in July in Japan. SUPER EXCITED!!!!!

item.title: A few months have passed since I was thinking about why I can't write a blog.
item.description:

item.content:
Most of us know the saying, Sticks and stones may break my bones, but words will never hurt me. However, this statement may not hold true for those of us who have experienced hurtful name-calling. If you have been called names or seen someone who has, you know how damaging these words can be. When it comes to name calling, many teens or children may not understand that name calling is also a form of bullying. They might start out by joking, but calling someone a name with the intent of hurting them is not okay.

Unfortunately, I know firsthand just how much damage name-calling can do. As a child, I experienced name-calling in my primary school years from both my peers and even my professor. Every day it seemed like there was a new insult hurled my way, and it felt like I had no escape from the constant barrage of negativity. Even though it started as jokes, it quickly turned into a form of bullying that left me feeling helpless and alone.

Name-calling is just one form of bullying, but it can be just as damaging as physical or cyberbullying. Verbal bullying can have a significant impact on a person’s mental and emotional wellbeing, causing low self-esteem, anxiety, depression, and even suicidal thoughts. And unlike physical bullying, the effects of verbal bullying can often go unnoticed by those around us.

It’s important to recognize that words have power, and the things we say can have a lasting impact on others. That’s why it’s crucial to speak out against name-calling and other forms of verbal bullying. Whether you’re a victim of name-calling yourself or you witness it happening to someone else, it’s important to take action and stand up for what’s right. In my case, my mom tried to talk to my professor about the name-calling, but unfortunately, nothing was ever done to address the issue. This made me feel even more helpless and alone, and I didn’t know where to turn. Fast forward almost two decade later, I’m 26 years old, yet here I am, suddenly finding myself crying over videos about bullying. I thought I was over it. But the cuts of bullying run deeper than I thought. They say that teenhood is pivotal to one’s life. It’s when our innocence begins to fade and we start seeing life’s many colors. It’s when our sense of identity is born, when we discover who we are and what we want to be.

Contrary to what a lot of people think, victims usually blame themselves more than anyone. They blame themselves for being weak, for not being popular, for not looking good enough, for not being white, for not being born to a more privileged side of the world, etc. This is because we grow up in a society that tells us that this is an eat-or-be-eaten world. We grow up in a society that tells us that being weak is a sin, and that nobody else is to be blamed for this but yourself. Never mind that the world is already unequal as it is, that some people are already being discriminated on the basis of their race, color, and gender. What bullies sees as just “having fun” makes people look down on themselves and not see their worth. It breaks confidence, harms reputations, and undermines one’s ability to perform.

The trauma cuts deep and the scars stay for a long time.

Remember the human

Remember the human who’s behind that social media profile. Remember the human who is your classmate and is probably having a hard time making friends. Remember the human who is your neighbor, the one who’s hating himself for having dark skin, acne, and curly hair. Remember the human in your friend who might not have the courage to tell you that he or she is hurting when you jokingly call her fat and ugly. Remember that you are human too.

I was inspired to write this blog after seeing in the news about a young person who suffered bullying. It hit close to home for me, as I too experienced bullying as a child. Watching the video brought back painful memories of the hurtful words and name-calling that I endured, and made me realize just how damaging this kind of behavior can be. That’s why I feel it’s important to speak out against name-calling and other forms of bullying, and to raise awareness about the lasting impact that they can have on a person’s mental and emotional wellbeing.

item.content:
Friendship and solitude

Amidst a period characterized by a pandemic, financial downturn, remote work and social distancing, relationships have been tested.

It is widely believed that a rise in divorce rates is imminent. This is not surprising, as financial difficulties can put a strain on a marriage, and also couples these days have to spend more time… with each other. Today, however, I would like to focus on our wider social circles and friendships. More precisely, I want to reflect on the potential advantages of being a loner.

Pandemic friendships: the orchid and the cactus

As humans, it is natural for us to seek social connections. However, with many living a simplified version of our previous lives, we may find ourselves reevaluating the nature and quality of our relationships. The people we choose to build relationships with have always been significant, but now we are becoming more aware of the impact these choices can have on our lives.

During this time, many friendships have either ended or evolved. Some have dissolved due to conflicting political or pandemic-related beliefs, while financial struggles may have slowly eroded others. Furthermore, some friends who we thought were close may have revealed themselves to be mere acquaintances, as the fun activities we once enjoyed together no longer mask our lack of true connection. In this virtual world, with just a Zoom screen to connect us, any incongruity in our relationships becomes more apparent.

Some friendships are like an orchid: Initially, they may appear appealing and promising, but in reality, they can be delicate and unpredictable. They require specific conditions and care to thrive, and even slight changes can cause them to wither away. For instance, overwatering or providing too much light can harm them. If not given enough attention, they may not last long. These relationships tend to prioritize aesthetics over substance and can feel a bit performative.

Maintaining an orchid friendship is a delicate process, and deep down, you are aware that it could easily fall apart even with the slightest mishap. It requires constant attention and effort, and any wrong move could potentially damage the relationship irreparably.

Some friendships are more like cactus. They are resilient, adaptable, and can withstand harsh environments. They’ll be with you forever.

But as the orchids have separated themselves from the cacti, I’m prompted to wonder: What about being a loner? Is it necessary to spend a lot of time socializing with friends to be happy and well-adjusted?

“Hell is other people.” – Jean-Paul Sartre

There are those who would identify with Sartre’s perspective and argue in favor of the loner life, which could involve having a small circle of friends or no friends at all.

It is important to note that chronic loneliness has been linked to physical harm, increasing our probability of early death, affecting our immunity, stress, sleep, cognitive functioning and mental health. However, it is crucial to distinguish between loneliness and the act of being alone for our purposes.

Can the loner enjoy being alone without being lonely, with only a few or no friends, and still maintain a high level of happiness?

The Stoic view

Seneca wrote a letter in which he discusses the common misinterpretation of the Stoic idea that “the wise man is content with himself.” While it may appear to be a motto for those who prefer solitude, the true meaning behind this concept is often misunderstood.

According to Seneca, while this quote means you are self-sufficient and doesn’t depend on others to be happy, but it doesn’t mean that they don’t desire friendships. He refers to a Stoic mind as “invulnerable” or “above all suffering”, so if you lose a friend, you can move on from that relationship. But friendships can still provide pleasure, love, and an opportunity to practice the skill of friendship. Seneca believes that the more virtuous a person is, the more they should engage in friendships because they provide a mechanism for collaboration and personal development for everyone involved.

Friendships are wonderful additions to life, but you can’t define your happiness purely through others. Happiness is an inside job.

Spend time doing things that make you happy, whether it’s reading a good book, going for a walk, or trying out a new hobby. Surround yourself with positive people who uplift you and make you feel good about yourself. Focus on building your self-esteem and your sense of self-worth.

Remember, just because nobody has ever had a crush on you doesn’t mean that it will never happen. Keep an open mind and continue to work on yourself and your personal growth. The right person will come along at the right time, and in the meantime, focus on being the best version of yourself that you can be.

Maha Shivratri, the great night of Lord Shiva, is a festival celebrated by millions of people around the world. It is a time to honor and worship Lord Shiva, the god of destruction and transformation, and to seek his blessings for a prosperous and fulfilling life. The journey to Grand Bassin on Maha Shivratri is a unique experience that I have been fortunate enough to undertake multiple times. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the pilgrimage was not possible in 2021 and 2022, but with restrictions easing, I was excited to return to the road and experience the adventure once again. This year, I decided to start my walk from Rose Belle, which added an extra dimension of excitement to the journey. Although I did not take many pictures this year, I will be sharing some from my previous journey to give you a glimpse of the pilgrimage.

Walking through the night, surrounded by the beauty of Mauritius, is a one-of-a-kind experience that I look forward to each year. The camaraderie of fellow travelers, the delicious food and drink, and the spiritual significance of the journey all contribute to an unforgettable adventure. As we made our way through the darkness, we were joined by people from all over the island who were making their way to Grand Bassin on foot. As we walked, we were sustained by the generosity of the people of Mauritius. Along the way, we were offered food and drink from temples and from people’s homes. It was a heartwarming reminder of the kindness and hospitality that permeates this island nation. The food was all free of charge, provided by those who wanted to contribute to the pilgrimage and help make the journey a little easier for their fellow travelers. It was a beautiful expression of community spirit, and one of the many reasons why the Maha Shivratri pilgrimage is such a special experience. The sense of community and shared experience was palpable, and as the night wore on, our feet grew heavy, but our spirits remained high. With my backpack, comfortable sandals, and a sense of anticipation, I set out once again to see where the journey would take me.

Preparations

Before embarking on the journey, it’s important to understand the route and what to expect along the way. The pilgrimage to Grand Bassin typically starts from various locations across the island and converges at the sacred lake. For my journey, I decided to start from Rose Belle. Below is a map of the route we took, which covers a distance of approximately 20 kilometers.

The terrain is mostly hilly, with some steep inclines and declines, so it’s essential to wear comfortable footwear. By preparing adequately and knowing what to expect, we were able to make the most of our pilgrimage experience. Since the journey took place at night, I made sure to bring a jacket with me as a precautionary measure against the cold weather. Temperatures can drop significantly at night, and I didn’t want to risk getting sick.

The Walk

As I live in Mahebourg, a group of my friends and I decided to take the bus from there to Rose Belle. We met up with some other friends at Rose Belle at aorund 4pm, and we began our journey on foot. Walking through the bustling streets, we were surrounded by the festive atmosphere, as people from all over the island were making their way to Grand Bassin.

Here’s a picture of Manish, Bhavana, and me taken in 2020, just before we started our walk.

As we made our way, I caught up with a school friend of mine whom I hadn’t seen in almost 15 years. It was a coincidence that we both work in the same company now, and we were both happy to reconnect after so many years. We talked about our time in school, reminisced about old times, and marveled at how much things had changed since then. We also laughed over some of our old memories. and joked along the way, and it was great to be able to share this journey with old friends. We also talked about our friends from primary school, some of which are already married and now have children of their own, while we were still single.

We were a large group of walkers, and as we progressed, everyone started to separate. Some were ahead, while some were way behind. However, we continued to support and encourage each other along the way. One of the most memorable aspects of the journey was the food. We stopped at various food stalls along the way, where we savored some of the most delicious street food Mauritius has to offer, such as roti, puri, briyani, and lots of juice and tea. The vendors were friendly and welcoming, and the food was freshly prepared, giving us a taste of the local cuisine.

Our group stopped to eat, and as a big fan of biryani, I couldn’t resist getting myself a plate.

As the journey progressed, we started to feel the strain on our feet. The constant walking and the weight of our backpacks were taking a toll on our bodies. However, we took breaks along the way, sitting down to rest and rejuvenate. At times, we took longer breaks, and we could feel our feet struggling to get back up. But with each other’s support, we managed to push through.

We continued to walk through the night, and finally, around midnight, we arrived at Grand Bassin. The sight of the sacred lake and the temple of Lord Shiva was awe-inspiring, and we felt a sense of accomplishment and fulfillment.

Here’s a photo of our complete group taken in 2020 at Grand Bassin, once we had made it to our destination."

item.content:
I’ve been doing a lot of thinking about my relationship with social media. Over the years, I’ve struggled between enjoying it’s benefits while also watching it consume valuable time that I will never get back. I would take social media breaks, in the hopes that I would be able to have more control over my time while still being active on the platforms. The problem was that I kept coming back and getting sucked into the same cycle of consumption over creation.

Last year, I came across a few personal websites/blogs which made me re-think my usage of social media. They made me ask questions like:

  • What is my intention behind using social media?
  • How do I want to utilize my attention on a daily basis?

Eventually, I set out to answer these questions and began to think more and more about the intention behind many things that I do, not just with my time and attention on social media, but in life overall. So much so, that I think my word of the year for 2023 will be intention. What could be more crucial than how I spend my time when my life could end tomorrow? I seriously doubt that when I look back on my life, I’ll be reminiscing on the tweets and Instagram posts that I liked. I want to be able to look back and recall ideas that I brought to fruition, the creative ways in which I engaged with the world, and the like-minded individuals I met along the way.

In today’s mainstream society, when we are inundated with a plethora of media and opinions vying for our attention, living as many moments as one can manage with intention may seem like an impossible task. I know one thing for certain – I can’t continue siphoning my attention towards the addictive aspects of social media.

  • Addiction

Social media is naturally made to be addictive.

Over the past 10 years, social media has been finetuned to work against you and to push for your attention.

  • Social Media Impacts the Whole World

Most people use social media, it impacts a very large aspect of the world.

Most social media generally has an “algorithm” to promote content. This algorithm is always being balanced and modified ever so slightly.

They modify it to make people think certain ways, or to promote certain types of content over others. Effectively giving them the ability to brainwash the world.

Look at those Tiktok challenges. No other platform promoted these challenges as much as Tiktok. It convinced people to do stupid things that they wouldn’t have done otherwise.

It even got to the point that schools had to shutdown.

  • Not Being in Control Over Content

How are you not in control? You get to choose who you follow. Yep you do, but I constantly get crap in my feed that I don’t want to see.

Things that I don’t follow get forced in my face no matter what.

I want to be in control of the things that I get to see on social media.

In my opinion it would be best just to be connected with your friends and family. I don’t care about the celebrities and all the other junk that gets thrown in my face.

  • Being a Hypocrite

I don’t support where social media is headed, and how manipulative it’s getting.

Therefore, I will not use it. Under normal circumstances

  • Why I Kinda Use Social Media

A year ago I deleted my Instagram/Facebook/Whatsapp account. Here’s my philosophy that led to me deleting it.

If you don’t support it, don’t use it.

You know, basically don’t be a hypocrite.

Since then, I missed seeing what my friends are up to and connecting to them through that. So it’s hard to support both, you know? I don’t want to support Facebook by using Instagram, but I want to support my friends by seeing and messaging with them on the platform.

So I decided to get back on the platform. But I have a specific way of going about things that screws over Facebook and Instagram 😂

The Solution

I won’t post on Instagram. I will instead be using my blog.

Posts on my microblog will be similar to how I would post on Instagram. I will keep my blog seperate, because my posts there will be more technical and informational.

Anyways, social media is messy and big tech is making it a terrible platform to be on. Social media isn’t all bad, it’s definitely being used for good. But the platforms are designed to work against you for your attention. So it’s best to have alternative ways of reaching others, not just through social media.

item.content:
The most important choice in life is not to choose what kind of work to do, nor to choose which company to invest in, but to choose who to marry.

The first time I heard this statement came from Bill Gates and Buffett. Of course, the two of them are good friends and and the possibility of mutual influence cannot be ruled out，but I believe this is a common choice for all wise men. They all believe that the most important thing in life is not which company to invest in, but who to marry.

To further explain his point of view, Buffett told his own story. He said he was dating the most beautiful girl in the state when she was young, but in the end he did not choose to be with her. He said: This girl has been divorced three times. If she is with me, I don’t know what the result will be.

No matter who you are, where you are, what kind of work you are doing, famous or ordinary, the eternal topic for individuals is life itself, the ones who accompany you the longest in this life are neither your parents, nor your children, nor Not your colleagues, but your partner. Therefore, from a time perspective, the choice of a partner is the most important choice in life.

From another perspective, if we perform well in other aspects of life, such as education, career, investment, and financial management, etc., we have made the right choices and achieved proud results, but if we choose the wrong partner, This failed relationship would render all of the above options moot.

For example, if a person is very successful in his career, and his career achievements far exceed those of his peers, but he is not wise enough in his choice of marriage, then a fire in his backyard is enough to destroy everything he has worked hard for many years. There are also entrepreneurs, whose wife divorces on the eve of the company’s listing, which is enough to ruin a successful IPO, so that all investors must investigate the marital status of the founder when deciding whether to invest in a company afterwards.

Therefore, no matter how good a person is in other areas, if he is always foolish in the choice of feelings and marriage, we think he is lacking in great wisdom in life—because he lacks in the most important things in life. Judgment, not knowing what he wants in life, this may reflect that he may not be good at long-term thinking.

When you consider a lifelong partner, you may wish to think about a question: If there is one most important factor that makes you both have the courage to choose to be together, what is this factor?

There is an unexpected answer: to break up well, to make each other better, not to destroy each other.

People often say: Human nature cannot stand the test. But think about it the other way around: only what can stand the test is human nature. What is the biggest test between a couple? It is to see how they will deal with the breakup. It’s a love affair in the heart, but they are still willing to break up peacefully, or they still want to hurt each other, or even destroy each other.

Of course, many people will ask:

First, before I choose to be with someone, how can I see each other’s state when facing (if) breaking up?

Second, I am choosing a life partner. Why should I think about such an unlucky topic: breaking up?

My answer is: First of all, you can observe this person from various angles, including how they usually treats friends, differences, contradictions, and “injustice”. It even includes how did they deal with the previous relationship, how did they break up with Ex? If a person is full of complaints or even resentment towards Ex, then don’t expect Ta to treat the “breakup” peacefully in the future.

Secondly, there is an analogy as to why it is necessary to judge how a person will face a “breakup” before deciding to fall in love or even be together: that is, if we understand how we will face death in our daily life, it will completely change our life. Life. Although it is difficult for us to face the topic of “death” and choose to avoid it in our daily life, once we have the courage to face the topic of death and have a little breakthrough cognition here, our life will be greatly improved. For a different self. This point was brilliantly elaborated by Jobs in his most famous speech during his lifetime: “Three Stories of My Life”. He said that the best teacher in life is “death”. After he was diagnosed with cancer for the first time, he really understood the “meaning of death”. He said:

“Remember that I am going to die” is the most important mantra I have encountered in my life, and it helped me make important choices in my life.

By analogy, if lovers can think about how they will break up before deciding to be together. If both can accept each other’s attitude towards breaking up, then the relationship between the two of them will be much stronger. When we think about breaking up and talking about breaking up, we don’t plan to break up one day in the future, but pass the limit test of “breakup” to judge a person’s bottom line in dealing with feelings.

If this test can be passed, if it is determined that everyone can treat each other with sincerity and achieve mutual success when they may face a breakup in the future, then I think this couple has the most important foundation for a happy life together. When you know that you will not choose to hurt each other in the most difficult time, but choose to trust each other, then you will work together to overcome many difficulties in life.

We literally stayed up all night just to finish it. The project was an Android app that can be used to detect any infringement on the road while you’re driving. Feel free to contact me if you want more info; in any case, here’s my [research paper] (https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-90618-4_18).

Here’s a picture of me holding my dissertation (yes, this is my face). ugly? I know):

First Job

My first job was at Ceridian as an application analyst. During that time, I actually had no idea which career path to go down. You see, if you’re a techie, you know how big the tech world is, and unfortunately for me, I went with the first company that contacted me, which was, of course, Ceridian.The job was basically like a call center. I am sorry if you’re from Ceridian and are reading this, but I absolutely hated my job. It stinks, despite the fact that the salary was excellent for an entry-level employee like me. See, they had an application called DayForce, while the app is game changing in the HR world, my job was mainly to resolve issues that clients faced. And yes, if you’re guessing by now, I only worked on Dayforce. During the three months, I adapted rather quickly, but the longer I stayed at the job, the more I realized that I was only learning the application for the company. I’m not actually learning anything; there are no new technologies. At one point, we were getting training on all sorts of HR-related stuff.

As I said in my previous blog, even though I’m an introvert, I often like to listen to people, especially older people, as I get to hear about their experiences with their mistakes. Opinions from some people serve as an excellent warning sign what not to do. Listen to genuine people who lived their lives and had careers. E.g. never take advice on parenting from someone who is 25 and have no kids. Do not take relationships advice from someone who had never been in at least mid-term relationships. Do not listen to what to read or watch or to do from such people. Listen to people who are nice, and lived their lives and also are always changing. Self-righteous people change very slowly. Because they already have all the “answers.” Be open to the ideas, but really think who are you talking to now. Bad advice is much worse than no advice at all!

So I did. I talked to the system administrators there, who told me being in my current job would get me nowhere if I’m someone who loves to learn. Interestingly, during that time, they were hiring for the post of configuration management. But the mistake I made was telling my manager I hated the job. I know what you’re thinking: “Girish, why did you do that?” Frankly, I don’t know, I so hated my job that I wanted to quit asap. So, I told him, there is an opening for configuration management, and I want to apply for it. So he did his best. I got an interview, which was great, I was so hopeful that I would get it. After one week, I did not get it. I was told that I did not have enough experience for the job and did not have ccna too. That was my first encounter with depression, which hit me really hard. I was really down during these times, and I was also getting pressured by management and HR.

In my opinion, it is still important to listen and reflect on this advice and opinions. But mostly as an exercise in reflection. Opinions from some people serve as an excellent warning sign what not to do.

Before we continue, here are some happy memories I had at Ceridian.

This was during the eoy party with my two work buddies.

Another selfie, this time with my mentor, who has really helped me since day 1. Since he was a huge Game of Thrones fan, I gave him a Game of Throne Msic Box for Christmas for really helping, teaching, and mentoring me. 

Okay, so last image. This was the drunken team. I don’t remember how much I drank that night, but it was insane, the best eoy party I’d ever been to. I do remember the guys from the system admin team giving me Jack Daniels to drink. Yeah, crazy night. And let’s not forget the walk of shame when I went back to work. I received a lot of compliments. I’m someone who will actually forget about everything when I get on the dance floor. Get me drunk and get me on the dance floor, and you sure will have a night you’ll always remember!

Let’s get back to the boring stuff, shall we? After getting pressured by the manager, I started applying for other jobs. I eventually got a job interview with SD Worx as a system administrator. I did 3 interviews (2 technical ones and 1 HR). Another major blunder I made at Ceridan was submitting my resignation letter before finding another job. So yeah, this happened, I was so sure I was going to get the job at SD worx that I gave my resignation letter early. Yes, I did not get it, and I was left with no job after I left Ceridian. To make things worse, it was during that time that COVID hit.

Depression phase

The thing about Depression is it kind of collapses time. Suddenly, you find your whole days blending together to create one endless and suffocating loop. So you find yourself trying to remember the things that made you happy. But slowly, your brain begins to erase every memory that ever brought you joy. And eventually, all you can think about is how life has always been this way. An will only continue to be this way. Someone once said that these states will wax and wane. Which gave my mother relief, because it meant that in the bad times, there would be good times. But it also gave her anxiety because it meant that in the good times, there would be bad times. It always confused me, because I didn’t really know what it meant. But it did sound a lot calmer than the way I would describe it. Granted, I didn’t realize until later what waxing and waning implied. That these feelings were fixed and constant and would never end for the rest of my life.

For nearly six months, I was unemployed. Full mode depression I went through a lot of stuff during these periods, having nightmares every day. It was awful, I must say. especially since the lockdown. staying at home, sleeping all day. There were times when I nearly gave up. I was filled with negative thoughts. What kept me sane was anime/manga. I spend most of my time reading manga and books. During these times also, I only stayed in contact with one friend (we didn’t talk for nearly a year, she was kind of an angel sent from the sky to cheer me up). She was always supportive, always encouraging me not to give up. Also, my parents are always looking out for me. And I did; I started to get back in shape. I began to take my career seriously. I applied to a bunch of companies. I got a lot of rejections but never gave up.

Eventually I got an interview at Linkbynet. Lockdown periods were over, so I went and did the technical interview. It was fun; I prepared a lot for this. They did ask me why I was unemployed, and I just kept true to myself and told them about my current situation, why I left the job at Ceridian, and the stuff I’m having to go through. And three days later, I got the job as a junior system administrator. The only issue was that I had to wait another three months to start the job. So I did.

During these three months, I started preparing for my new job. I started learning Linux, System Administrator job. Since my friend was having some issues with her final year project, I kept myself busy.

One of the best achievements of my life was assembling a huge team of 23 people during Cyclone Class 3 to go play laser tag. Yes, I think it was a Sunday; I’m not sure, but 23 people during Cyclone class 3 was nearly an impossible task. Actually, it was class 2 in the morning, and we were still debating whether to go or not. Eventually, we decided to go since the weather was fine. It was only during the ride on the bus that we heard that it had become class 3. I called Funzone (RIP now) immediately to make sure if it would still operate, and luckily it did. Since it was located at 4 Bornes, we walked from Shoprite to 4 Bornes. Yeah, yeah. Not only did I make them come play laser tag, but they also walked nearly 30 minutes during Cyclone class 3. But hey, we had a lot of fun, and it’s something we’ll always remember. Here’s the awesome team:

Second Job

My second job was at Linkbynet (which is now Accenture), which was located in Phoenix, Les hailles. I integrated a team of Junior System admin. The job was okayish but boring since we were doing the same thing every day, like checking if inventory for both Linux and Windows failed or not and checking for any failed patching tickets. Boring, but I eventually learned a lot, and I also developed a script to get all patching tickets from an API to add the data to an Excel sheet. Each sheet represented one client. The script was written in Python and was run every Monday. I also took advantage of the free Azure Certification.It really was a fun experience. I remember doing an exam at 1 a.m. on a Saturday.

After nearly a year of completing all of these certifications, I became a Linux system administrator. Unfortunately, I did not get the team I wanted, but I entered a team called SSCR. The team was all about procedures. We have to follow a procedure for every job we do; it stinks, but we can’t do anything else. Despite all that, I managed to learn a lot of new technologies: Ansible, Terraform, and Kubernetes (although I still have a lot to learn).
